SWCCG sets are grouped into four eras: [[Decipher era|Decipher]], [[Virtual Original]], [[Virtual Legacy]] and [[Virtual Modern]]. The tables distinguish released expansions, supplemental products and planned material. Each era article also explains its history and card pool.

There is no Death Star II Sealed Deck; [[Death Star II Light Side Starter Deck]] and [[Death Star II Dark Side Starter Deck]] released with [[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]].<ref>[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

== [[Decipher era]] ==

Decipher sold booster expansions alongside fixed-card products, sealed-deck boxes and anthology collections. The anthologies introduced preview or premium cards while bundling packs and starters from earlier releases.<ref name="decipher-collection">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/thecollection/index.html Star Wars CCG: The Expansions], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990504174938id_/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/thecollection/index.html Internet Archive].</ref>

The Decipher card counts distinguish new cards, alternate images, foil subsets and game aids. A starter row gives the number of cards in a deck. Random reprints packed with Reflections or premium products do not increase their listed set sizes.<ref name="decipher-collecting">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], collecting catalog, pp. 4–45 and 201–202. The primary release notices for the later dates have not yet been located. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828id_/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

=== Cancelled and planned sets ===

Decipher announced four further expansions after [[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]], with the planned dates below.<ref name="decipher-planned">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/whatisit/afterdeathstar.html After Death Star II], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050307015419id_/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/whatisit/afterdeathstar.html Internet Archive].</ref>
The later [[Reflections Gold]] project also remained unreleased. In January 2002, [[Warren Holland]] announced that Lucasfilm had refused a proposed free PDF of 200 approved cards.<ref name="decipher-gold">Warren Holland, [http://www.decipher.com/starwars/reflectionsgold.html Star Wars Reflections Gold Announcement], Decipher (25 January 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20080207033202id_/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/reflectionsgold.html Internet Archive].</ref>
[[Reflections Gold Remastered]] is an independent remastered edition documented alongside the surviving original playtest material on [[Reflections Gold]].

== [[Virtual Original]] ==

The numbered sequence contains seventeen sets. [[Virtual Set: Defensive Shields]] is a separate supplemental sheet. The cards are printable [[V-slips]] used with their underlying [[Decipher]] cards. Early sheets identify when they became tournament-legal. Later revisions to the sheets retain their numbered set identities. Card totals count physical cards in the cited edition; the two faces of an Objective count as one card.<ref name="era-2eebf0f407">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualCards9.pdf VirtualCards9.pdf], Players Committee, release sheet. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195543/https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualCards9.pdf Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="era-41a77369bf">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050829203847id_/http://www.swccgpc.com/virtualcards.htm Virtual Cards download list, 29 August 2005], Players Committee.</ref>

== [[Virtual Legacy]] ==

The [[2009 Virtual Block Reorganization]] grouped earlier sets into themed Blocks. Blocks 1–5 are listed below. [[Virtual Block 6|Block 6]], [[Virtual Block 7|Block 7]], [[Virtual Block 8|Block 8]] and [[Virtual Block 9|Block 9]] have separate named releases, grouped under their parent Block. [[Virtual Shields]] is the Legacy shield package. The earlier [[Virtual Set: Defensive Shields|Original-era Defensive Shields]] is a different set. Totals count distinct physical cards in the cited sheets: two Objective faces count once, while alternate-image printings are shown separately. Duplicate cutouts and oversized layouts do not add cards.<ref name="era-c0fe78c57e">[https://web.archive.org/web/20090918131415id_/http://www.starwarsccg.org/ 16 September 2009 Reflections IV completion and realignment announcement], Players Committee.</ref>

=== Planned material ===

[[Twilight Of The Republic (Virtual Block 9)|Twilight Of The Republic]] was prepared as the second [[Virtual Block 9]] release. Its dated PDF is a surviving planned sheet. The [[2014 Virtual Card Pool Reset]] announcement said the release would not appear in that form.

== [[Virtual Modern]] ==

The numbered sequence begins with [[Virtual Set 0]], released after the [[2014 Virtual Card Pool Reset]], and continues through [[Virtual Set 27]]. [[Virtual Set D]] collects defensive shields. [[Virtual Set P]] collects premium cards released in two waves. Printable cards are available as [[V-slips]].<ref name="modern-releases">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/resources/virtual-slips/ Virtual Slips / Files]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261113162743/https://swccg.com/snapshots/pc/virtual-slips-20261113.html Internet Archive], Players Committee, release dates and printable sets (checked 13 November 2026).</ref>

The dates below are the original release dates. Card totals count distinct Light Side and Dark Side entries in the official rosters on 13 November 2026, with alternate images and both faces of a card counted once. Later additions, replacements and withdrawals can change a roster. The Set P wave rows instead count the four and three original cards of each release; the other premium items and alternate-image presentations remain catalogued on [[Virtual Set P]].
